title: G-code fundamentals: reading a 20-line facing program line by line
summary: A real ~20-line facing program on a mill, walked line by line so each word earns its place.

blocks.eyebrow: Read the tape before you press Cycle Start
blocks.title: Twenty lines that face a part
blocks.body: Facing is the simplest useful milling program: flatten the top of a billet. Below is a complete example program, then a line-by-line reading. Units are inches; the dialect is a common Fanuc-ish subset.

items.label: Work offset — top center of stock as Z0 example below uses top as Z0
Flat end mill in T1 / H1

blocks.heading: Lines 1–7: identity, safe modes, tool, spindle
blocks.body: O1001 names the program. The modal safety line cancels cutter comp, tool length cancel leftovers, canned cycles, and sets absolute mode in inches. G54 selects the work offset. T1 M06 puts the half-inch end mill in the spindle. G43 H1 applies tool length offset and parks Z at 1.0 above the offset. S3500 M03 spins clockwise; M08 turns coolant on.

blocks.heading: Lines 8–10: approach and first touch
blocks.body: Rapid to X-1.75 Y-0.75 — off the left edge of a 3-inch-wide billet centered on X0, below the near edge. Rapid Z to 0.1 clear. Feed to Z0.0 at 10 ipm to touch the face height. That first feed down is deliberate: never rapid into the material.

blocks.heading: Lines 11–17: the raster face
rows: First pass across the face at Z0
0.5" step for a 0.5" cutter ≈ full width; tighten if finish demands
Bidirectional facing to save air time
Cover the 2" depth of the billet with overlap
blocks.caption: Alternating X directions with Y step-overs is a classic face pattern. Finish passes often use a smaller step and climb milling only — this example favors clarity over polish.

blocks.heading: Lines 18–23: clear, stop, go home
blocks.body: Rapid Z to 1.0 clear. Coolant off (M09), spindle stop (M05). G91 G28 Z0 returns Z through machine home in incremental mode; G90 restores absolute. M30 ends and rewinds. If your control prefers G53 or a different home sequence, swap only the parking block — leave the cutting logic alone until you understand it.

blocks.heading: Words you just watched do work

nodes.title: G00 / G01
nodes.detail: Rapid versus linear feed — never confuse them near stock.

nodes.title: G90 / G91
nodes.detail: Absolute versus incremental. Mixing them without noticing is a classic crash story.

nodes.title: G43 Hn
nodes.detail: Tool length compensation — wrong H offset faces air or the vise.

nodes.title: M06 / M03 / M08 / M30
nodes.detail: Tool change, spindle CW, coolant on, program end.

blocks.heading: Before Cycle Start on a real machine

items.label: Work offset Z0 matches the program's assumption
items.detail: This example treats top of stock as Z0. If your shop zeros the table, rewrite Z.

items.label: Tool length H1 measured for the tool in the spindle
items.detail: A borrowed length offset faces the wrong plane.

items.label: Single-block the first approach with the door shut
items.detail: Prove rapids and the first feed down before full auto.

items.label: Confirm stock actually measures ~3×2 in the vise
items.detail: The X/Y extents are written for that blank.

blocks.title: Dialects differ; the reading skill transfers
blocks.body: Haas, Fanuc, Siemens, and conversational controls spell some parking and coolant codes differently. The point of this page is to read each word as a promise to the machine — not to memorize one builder's macro set.

blocks.heading: Line reading check
blocks.prompt: In the program above, what does G00 Y-0.25 do after a cutting pass?
options: Cuts a finishing pass at feed rate
Rapids in Y to the next step-over without cutting
blocks.explanation: G00 is rapid motion. Moving Y between X cutting passes positions the cutter for the next face stroke without feeding through material.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct — rapid step-over, then G01 cuts again.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Look at the modal group: G00 versus G01. Only G01 is cutting feed here.

blocks.heading: What this tiny program teaches versus what it skips

columns.name: Included
columns.detail: Safety modals, tool change, length offset, spindle/coolant, approach, raster face, park, end.

columns.name: Skipped on purpose
columns.detail: Cutter radius comp, canned cycles, subprograms, probing, adaptive clearing — learn those after you can read a face.

blocks.title: Modals remember until cancelled
blocks.body: G01 stays in effect until another motion modal replaces it. That is why a forgotten G00 after a cut can feed rapidly into the next move — or why a leftover G91 can turn a small number into a surprise. Read the modal state, not only the line in isolation.

blocks.heading: How the X/Y numbers were chosen
items: Stock is 3.0" in X and 2.0" in Y, centered near X0 Y0 for the example.
A 0.5" end mill needs to start off the left edge — hence X-1.75 for a cut that fully clears X±1.5.
Y step-overs of 0.5" with passes at -0.75, -0.25, 0.25, 0.75 cover ±1.0" with overlap.
If your blank is larger, extend the X strokes and add Y passes before you change feeds.

slides.title: Rapid above
slides.body: Tool sits at Z1.0, then rapids in X/Y to the start corner while still clear of the part.

slides.title: Feed to Z0
slides.body: Only the Z approach uses feed. This is the moment single-block earns its keep.

slides.title: Cut +X
slides.body: G01 across the face at the facing feed. Chips should look even; a squeal means something else is wrong.

slides.title: Step Y, cut −X
slides.body: Rapid Y, feed back. Repeat until the far edge is covered, then retract Z and shut down cleanly.

blocks.heading: Next practice
blocks.body: Change the Y step-over and the X extents on paper, then predict the toolpath before you simulate. Reading beats copying.
